body:
So far a maxLimit has been required for security purposes. You can set it to a very large number though (999999 etc).
But we could make it work for null as well if we want to.
The fix would be needed to be done in https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/2.x/lib/Cake/Controller/Component/PaginatorComponent.php#L425
@dereuromark I think zero for unlimited would be the expected behavior by most developers. Null on an integer parameter is kind of strange.

CakePHP is highly recommended that ignore the parameters when they are.

```
"límite" => null,  
"límite" => '', 
'límite' => 0,
or
'maxLimit' => null, 
'maxLimit' => '', 
'maxLimit' => 0,
```

And take the default parameters for each of them.
Do not you think.? That way there is never a warning from PHP.

@dereuromark I absolutely agree.

If you need to **dump** your database. You shouldn't be using pagination.

Exactly, as such we just need to make sure we throw an exception if the maxLength value is < 1 :)
A PR from anyone would be very welcome.
We can also document this necessity.

I do to show all the data from the DB; because in that case I use **->find('all', ...).**
I only test to see if by an array merge, cakephp to detect invalid parameters was returning to the default values.

**Example:**
In this way a whole driver I use. limit => '350' and MaxLimit = '350' but in an action X always mind you step limit => null and MaxLimit => null or the like, so that the pager ignore it and take the default data page.

So I think I would have to clean cakephp not an exception. Since it would make no fexible in performance.?

... then do count and set maxlimit to your rowcount - for small tables this will work, for larger it will hit you hard (Edit: my brain is fried: just don't use pagination AT ALL)

... for exports and backups see bufferResults=false and streaming row by row
Does raising an exception on a limit/maxLimit of '', null, 0 sound reasonable? To me that feels like a NotFoundException as the thing you've asked for will never be found.
I would only go for maxLimit, as  limit 0 = none might be a valid DRY case to just respect the maxLimit and is currently already supported this way.
I'm not sure I follow how limit=0 is ever a productive thing to do.
AFAIK from looking at the code earlier, this basically means use/inherit maxLimit ;)

MaxLimit 0 Exception sounds sane if it helps.
limit = 0 => limit = maxLimit also sounds sane.

I think the same thing @markstory not have to be an "Exception". CakePHP has only to please ignore if "limit" and "MaxLimit" parameter is not valid and take those who are by default.
Or if you want you can also gener an error in the log file; but no Exception.

CakePHP ORM, just have to ignore if the parameters are not correct, when one overwrites it with arraymerge, so in that case to be NULL, take the defaults.

> I hope this clear idea through google traslartor.
@EOM Why wouldn't you want an exception. Silently ignoring programmer error is generally not how we handle those cases.
